text: Adult dogs typically eat twice a day, morning and evening, with portion size based on weight. Avoid grapes, chocolate, onions, and xylitol.
Puppies under six months need three to four small meals per day with puppy-formulated food rich in protein and DHA.
Cats are obligate carnivores. Feed wet or dry food twice daily. Always provide fresh water and avoid dog food, which lacks taurine.
Most adult dogs need at least thirty minutes of walking daily. High-energy breeds like huskies and border collies need one to two hours.
Never give human medication to pets without vet approval. Ibuprofen and acetaminophen are toxic to dogs and cats.
Healthy adult pets need a vet checkup once a year. Senior pets over seven and puppies/kittens need visits every six months.
Brush short-haired cats weekly and long-haired cats daily to prevent mats and reduce hairballs.
Bathe dogs every four to six weeks. Brush short coats weekly and double coats two to three times per week.
When tasks conflict, prioritize medications first, then feedings, then walks, then grooming. Medications are time-sensitive and should not be delayed.
Cats need fifteen to twenty minutes of active play twice daily. Use wand toys and laser pointers to keep them engaged.
